title: State Development, Infrastructure and Works Committee
speaker: Mrs Kirkland
passage: Mrs KIRKLAND (Rockhampton—LNP) (3.46 pm): I rise to speak on the State Development, Infrastructure and Works Committee report No. 15, Consideration of Auditor-General Report 5: 2024-25—Preparing for the Brisbane games. On 21 July 2021 the venue for the 2032 Olympic and Paralympic Games was announced, giving us a total of 11 years to prepare for the 2032 games. We had 11 years, but the previous Labor government muddled along for over 1,000 days and still had no credible delivery plan. As promised in the 2024 election campaign, in 100 days the now Crisafulli government delivered our Brisbane 2032 Olympic and Paralympic Games venues and infrastructure plan. This committee report has acknowledged what the Auditor-General and officers of the Queensland Audit Office briefed. The committee recommended that the Auditor-General continue to monitor governance structures over the life cycle of the games delivery program. It is important to note that this came out after our 100-day campaign.

The report highlights the importance of strong governance, clear accountability, effective risk management and responsible financial planning. We are focused on delivering the games responsibly, with every games related activity managed within approved budgets. All games entities have accepted the Auditor-General’s four recommendations, and work is underway to put them into action. This is another example of how our government gets on with delivering projects purposefully, methodically and with a clear plan. Our government does not just act; we listen and we welcome feedback. … … The Barlow Park upgrades will be delivered. The Cairns Convention Centre upgrades will be delivered. The Cairns Western Arterial Road will be delivered and fast-tracked in the lead-up to the games. Because we want Cairns to welcome athletes, visitors and the world, we need the infrastructure to support it. The Auditor-General’s report is an important part of that accountability, but we must also recognise the work undertaken since the audit, including the 2032 Delivery Plan, stronger governance arrangements and the agreement with the Commonwealth on the venue program. …
